end.summary:
Named common non-metals and identified several as solids or gases, including oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, carbon and iodine.
Connected graphite, chlorine, iodised salt, nitrogen fertilisers and chips packets with everyday uses.
Explained that oxygen helps cells release energy from food and supports breathing and burning.
Teach-back on why oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential to living things was not passed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised identifying non-metals, their states, and everyday uses. They explained the role of oxygen in breathing and energy release, and connected nitrogen with plant growth and fertilisers. They initially wondered whether oxygen is the gas used in chips packets; this was clarified later by identifying nitrogen as the relevant gas (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask them to sort five non-metals into solid, liquid or gas and give one use for each.
